name: Lady Elliot Island
description: Lady Elliot Island, the southernmost coral cay of the Great Barrier Reef, 85 km north-east of Bundaberg in a Green Zone of the Marine Park, with its reef and the open water around it. Manta rays are drawn to the plankton around the island. Rebuilt from 30 m survey bathymetry and Sentinel-2; the cay's ground is rebuilt from its mapped outline.
area_note: 12 x 12 km centred on the island: its platform reef (about 1.3 km across) and the open shelf around it, mostly 30-55 m deep. There is no other reef within the box; Lady Musgrave Island, the nearest, is 40 km north-west.

tide.note: Waddy Point (24 58 S 153 21 E) is on the open-ocean coast of K'gari, 114 km south-south-east. MSQ lists Lady Elliot Island as a secondary place of Bundaberg (Burnett Heads, 80 km south-south-west, at the mouth of the Burnett River) with high water 24 and low water 33 minutes earlier and 0.74 of its range. Waddy Point's tide runs about 25 minutes ahead of Burnett Heads' (M2 phase 12 degrees earlier in the 2026 fit), the same as Lady Elliot's, and its spring range about mean sea level (MHWS +0.63, MLWS -0.62 m) is closer to Lady Elliot's (+0.87, -0.86 m) than Burnett Heads' (+1.16, -1.17 m), so the open-coast gauge is the closer match. Heights at the island are still about a third larger than Waddy Point's.
